cards.name: Blocks
cards.summary: Breaks the image into a grid of rectangular blocks and pushes each block a random distance from its place, so the picture looks cut into scattered puzzle-like pieces with gaps between them; the gaps are filled according to FillMode (and ColorItem when a colour fill is chosen). Block ranges and defaults were not read by the harvest, so the demo values are a reasoned guess.
use_for: broken / shattered photo look behind a headline
collage or cut-up background panel for a poster
glitchy, fragmented transition still between two sections of a layout
avoid: small blocks with a small offset only roughen the image and read as a rendering fault: use clearly larger blocks
faces and small type: the offset tears features apart, so keep them out of the effect or mask them back in
a clean regular pixel grid with no displacement: use Pixelate instead

params.name: Block width
params.does: width of each block before it is moved
params.typical: larger values give fewer, bigger, more readable pieces (range not harvested)

params.name: Block height
params.does: height of each block
params.typical: same as width for square pieces

params.name: Square
params.does: unlabelled check box (key Square); presumably locks block height to block width (not verified)

params.name: Max. offset
params.does: the furthest a block may be pushed from its original position
params.typical: higher values open wider gaps and make the break obvious

params.name: FillMode
params.does: what shows in the gaps left between moved blocks (option values not harvested)
params.typical: the default; switch to a solid colour for a graphic look

params.name: ColorItem
params.does: the gap colour when FillMode is set to a colour fill

pairs_with: Pixelate (regular blocks without displacement)
Tile (repeat the image as a grid)
a duotone or Posterize pass on the pieces for a print look

review.changes: params: Square no longer asserted to lock height to width (caption-less check box, behaviour not harvested), hedged like the Tile card

verified.note: The plate is cut into a grid of rectangular blocks, each pushed a random distance, with white gaps between them (the dialog's stored fill), the scattered puzzle-piece look described; the 'dropped' list (all four keys) is not evidence here, because Blocks is random and its repeat-render noise (62) is as large as every key probe.

cards.name: Displace
cards.summary: Moves the image's pixels according to the light and dark values of a displacement map chosen from the dialog's list (CurrentDisplaceImage), so the picture takes on that map's texture, such as wavy glass or a rippled or blocky refraction. Horizontal and Vertical set how far pixels shift; the map is tiled or stretched over the image.
use_for: textured glass / refraction look over a background photo
distorting an image to follow a pattern for a stylised poster
subtle texture warp that breaks up a flat, digital-looking image
avoid: high Horizontal / Vertical values tear the image into unreadable streaks: stay low for faces and type
a precise bend along a drawn shape: use Mesh Warp or an envelope instead
scripts: the harvested map list (CurrentDisplaceImage) was empty with a blank default, so a script cannot pick a map and may apply none: choose the map in the dialog

params.name: ScaleMode
params.does: Tile repeats the map across the image at its own size; Stretch to fit scales one copy over the whole image
params.typical: Tile for fine texture, Stretch for one big distortion

params.name: Horizontal
params.does: how far pixels shift sideways for the map's brightness differences

params.name: Vertical
params.does: how far pixels shift up and down

params.name: Undefined Areas
params.does: fills the edges uncovered by the shift: Repeat Edges smears the border pixels, Wrap Around brings in pixels from the opposite side

params.name: CurrentDisplaceImage
params.does: the displacement map used, picked from the dialog's map list (the harvest found the list empty and the default blank)

pairs_with: Ripple or Swirl for a regular distortion instead of a map-driven one
a Gaussian blur on the map's result to soften torn edges
cards.scripting: shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("Displace", "DisplaceEffect ScaleMode=0,HorizontalScale=40,VerticalScale=40,UndefinedArea=0") (the form the render test used: enum keys go as their list index, captions are ignored: ScaleMode 0 Tile, 1 Stretch to fit; UndefinedArea 0 Repeat Edges, 1 Wrap Around)  // cdr_com: Shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect(UndoString, Command); key format from cmd_template, not applied in a test for this effect, so check the pixels changed; CurrentDisplaceImage left out: its list was empty and its default blank in the harvest, so which map a script uses (if any) is unknown
cards.non_destructive: yes from the Effects menu: CorelDRAW 2024 adds it to the object's effect stack (editable in the Properties docker); the scripted Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect path changes the bitmap itself

review.changes: avoid / params / scripting: dropped the claim that a script uses a 'default map'; the harvest read CurrentDisplaceImage as an empty list with a blank default

verified.note: The pixels are displaced by a tiled X-shaped (cross-hatch) map, so every edge, the mid-tones, swatches and type carry a repeating star-like refraction texture, the map-driven distortion the card describes with the dialog's stored map.

cards.name: Mesh Warp
cards.summary: Lays a grid of nodes over the image (Gridlines sets how many) and warps the picture like a rubber sheet as you drag those nodes in the dialog preview; the shape of the warp comes entirely from the hand-moved nodes or a saved preset. An untouched Default mesh presumably leaves the image unchanged.
use_for: bending a flat image or label to sit on a curved surface in a mock-up
freeform bulge / pinch of one part of a photo
playful hand-shaped distortion of a logo bitmap
avoid: unattended scripts: the node moves are made by hand in the dialog and are not harvested parameters, so a script with only Gridlines / Preset applies no visible distortion
regular, repeatable distortions: use Ripple, Swirl or Shear, which take numeric values
vector artwork that must stay vector: use an Envelope instead of a bitmap effect

params.name: Gridlines
params.does: number of grid lines (and so draggable nodes) across the image
params.typical: 4 (default) for broad bends, up to 10 for local control

params.name: Presets
params.does: loads a saved mesh shape; only Default was harvested (presumably the flat, undistorted mesh)

pairs_with: Envelope tool for vector objects
Perspective drop shadow or a lens to complete a mock-up
cards.scripting: shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("Mesh Warp", "MeshWarpEffect Gridlines=6,Preset=7cc7e96a-0171-4281-bc7f-b8c2bf4fab87")  // cdr_com signature; key format from cmd_template, not tested for this effect; node positions cannot be passed, so the result is presumably the unwarped Default mesh; menu GUID 4e45dd98-272e-4836-b154-f910327b74ea opens the dialog for hand editing
cards.non_destructive: yes from the Effects menu: CorelDRAW 2024 adds it to the object's effect stack (re-editable in the Properties docker)
cards.cost: light to apply; the cost is the manual node editing

review.changes: summary / Presets / scripting: 'Default = flat mesh, image unchanged' hedged as presumed (the harvest has only the preset label)

verified.note: Listed in gallery/cdr_effect/not_rendered.json (status 'needs_input' (only current cards are rendered)), so there is no frame to check.

second_opinion.note: Agree: listed in not_rendered.json by rule (status needs_input); harness check: no render was attempted, so there is no frame to misread and the card makes no frame-based claim.

cards.name: Offset
cards.summary: Shifts the whole image horizontally and vertically inside its own frame, by a percentage of its size (default) or by a fixed distance; the area uncovered by the shift is filled per Mode (for example wrapped round from the opposite edge or a colour from ColorItem). With wrap-around the image's edges meet in the middle as visible seams.
use_for: checking and fixing seams when building a seamless repeat pattern tile
re-centring a texture so its seam falls where it can be retouched
deliberate split / shifted-frame look for a glitch poster
avoid: moving an object on the page: just move or transform it, which keeps the full image
photos with a clear subject: the wrap-around seam cuts straight through it
Mode option values were not harvested, so a script can only rely on the default fill

params.name: Horizontal
params.does: sideways shift, -100 to 100 (positive and negative move opposite ways)
params.typical: 50 (default, half the width) to centre the seam

params.name: Vertical
params.does: up / down shift, -100 to 100

params.name: Shift value as % of dimensions
params.does: on: Horizontal / Vertical are percentages of the image size; off: absolute distances

params.name: Mode
params.does: how the uncovered area is filled (options not harvested)
params.typical: options and default not harvested; for pattern work pick wrap-around if the list offers it

params.name: ColorItem
params.does: fill colour when Mode uses a colour

pairs_with: Tile (to preview the repeat)
Clone / healing retouch on the centred seam in Corel PHOTO-PAINT

cards.non_destructive: yes from the Effects menu: CorelDRAW 2024 adds it to the object's effect stack; the scripted Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect path changes the bitmap itself

verified.note: The image is shifted 30 % right and 40 % down inside its frame and wrapped round: the dark-red block, swatch strip and type now sit across the top, part of the photo's centre appears at the left edge, and the wrapped edges meet as hard seams through the middle.

cards.name: Pixelate
cards.summary: Rebuilds the image from flat-coloured cells, each the average colour of the pixels it covers: square or rectangular blocks, or Radial cells arranged in rings around the centre. Width / Height set the cell size and Opacity blends the pixelated result over the original.
use_for: 8-bit / retro pixel-art look for a poster or thumbnail
censoring or anonymising a face, plate or text in a photo
radial pixel burst background for a tech or gaming layout
avoid: scripts: the harvest's apply test returned OK but changed no pixels with 'PixelateEffect Mode=Square,Width=8,Height=8,Opacity=100' (or Width 60), so the command string is not established; apply from the menu
very small cells on an already soft photo barely read: use cells of 20 px or more
real redaction of sensitive text: small cells can be partly reversed, so cover it with a solid box instead

params.name: Mode
params.does: cell shape: Square, Rectangular (independent width and height) or Radial (rings around the centre)

params.name: Width
params.does: cell width in pixels

params.name: Height
params.does: cell height in pixels (used by Rectangular and Radial)

params.name: Opacity
params.does: how strongly the pixelated cells cover the original

pairs_with: Posterize for a limited-palette pixel-art look
a mask or clip so only one area is pixelated
cards.scripting: shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("Pixelate", "PixelateEffect Mode=0,Width=40,Height=40,Opacity=100") (the form the render test used: enum keys go as their list index, captions are ignored: Mode 0 Square, 1 Rectangular, 2 Radial)  // cdr_com signature; NOT working in the harvest test (returned OK, no pixel change with Width 8 vs 60: command string not recognised). Untested alternatives: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("defc5eef-4402-4c64-8837-aa8c2e635456") opens the Effects/Distort/Pixelate dialog on the selection (a person sets values and presses OK), or the Properties docker toggle EffectsPropertiesDS;Path=ApplyOrDeleteEffect:PixelateEffect; read the pixels back after either
cards.non_destructive: yes from the Effects menu: CorelDRAW 2024 adds it to the object's effect stack (editable in the Properties docker)

review.changes: scripting: the menu GUID / docker toggle were called a 'Working route' but were never tested from a script; now marked untested, the GUID shown as an InvokeItem call that opens the modal dialog; 'keys not recognised' -> 'command string not recognised' (the batch's wording)

verified.note: The photo is rebuilt from square flat-colour cells (about 20 px in the 960 frame at Width 40), each the average of what it covers; Mode and Height were ignored by the script (dropped), so only the default Square mode is shown.

cards.name: Ripple
cards.summary: Bends the image with regular sine-like waves running in the direction set by Angle; Period is the distance between waves and Amplitude their strength. Perpendicular Wave adds a second wave set at right angles (its own Amplitude), and Distort ripple makes the waves irregular.
use_for: water-reflection or heat-haze look on a photo
wavy, psychedelic background for a music or party poster
flag-in-the-wind feel on a flat graphic
avoid: high amplitude on faces and type makes them unreadable: keep text out of the ripple or use low values
only the outline of vector shapes should wave: a vector effect (Distort tool Zipper with smooth option) keeps it vector
Optimize Speed can show jagged edges on final output: switch to Quality for the export

params.name: Period
params.does: distance between wave crests

params.name: Amplitude (Amplitude)
params.does: how far the main wave pushes pixels

params.name: Optimize
params.does: Speed renders faster, Quality gives smoother edges

params.name: Perpendicular Wave
params.does: adds a second wave at right angles to the first for a cross-hatched water look

params.name: Amplitude (PerpAmplitude)
params.does: strength of the perpendicular wave

params.name: Distort ripple
params.does: makes the waves irregular rather than evenly spaced
params.typical: on for a natural water look

params.name: Angle
params.does: direction the waves run across the image, in degrees

params.name: ImageNode
params.does: internal image-node selector of the dialog (values not harvested)

pairs_with: Swirl or Whirlpool for other liquid distortions
a blue duotone / colour balance for a water look

cards.non_destructive: yes from the Effects menu: CorelDRAW 2024 adds it to the object's effect stack; the scripted Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect path changes the bitmap itself

verified.note: Strong regular sine waves bend the whole plate: the colour strip, black band and dark-red blocks rise and fall in big smooth humps and the large shapes and stripes are bent along them (Period 40, Amplitude 35, Angle 90).

cards.name: Shear
cards.summary: Bends the image to follow a curve drawn in the dialog: with Vertical orientation the image is pushed left and right along a top-to-bottom curve, with Horizontal up and down along a left-to-right one; Scale sets how strong the bend is and Edges style fills the uncovered edges (ColorItem when a colour is used). The curve is shaped by hand with the Edit Style tools; which way each orientation bends and whether the Default preset bends the image at all are not confirmed by the harvest.
use_for: S-curve bend of a photo strip or banner for a dynamic layout
wavy, melted or swaying look on a single image
bending a bitmap logo along a gentle arc
avoid: scripts: the shear curve is drawn in the dialog and is not a harvested parameter, so a script cannot shape it
regular repeating waves: use Ripple, which takes numeric period and amplitude
vector shapes that must stay editable: use an Envelope or the Distort tool

params.name: Edit Style
params.does: how the shear curve is edited: Curve (smooth nodes), Straight (straight segments), Freehand (drawn), Gamma (single gamma-style curve)

params.name: Orientation
params.does: Vertical: the shear curve runs top to bottom and the image bends left-right along it; Horizontal: the curve runs across and the image bends up-down (direction not verified)

params.name: Scale
params.does: strength of the shear applied along the curve

params.name: Edges style
params.does: how the edges uncovered by the shift are filled (options not harvested)

params.name: ColorItem
params.does: edge fill colour when Edges style uses a colour

params.name: Presets
params.does: loads a saved curve; only Default was harvested

pairs_with: Ripple for regular waves
Envelope for vector bends

cards.name: Swirl
cards.summary: Twists the image around its centre into a spiral, rotating the middle the most and the edges least, like stirring paint; the total twist is Whole Rotations plus Additional Degrees, clockwise or counter-clockwise.
use_for: hypnotic spiral / vortex background for a poster
dreamy or dizzy transition still
abstract texture made by swirling a colourful photo
avoid: faces and type in the centre are twisted beyond recognition: keep them outside the effect
an even, whole-image rotation: use the Rotate transform instead
Optimize Speed can leave jagged spirals on export: use Quality for final output

params.name: Direction
params.does: spin direction of the spiral

params.name: Optimize
params.does: Speed renders faster, Quality gives smoother spirals

params.name: Whole Rotations
params.does: full turns added to the twist
params.typical: 0 (default) to 2; more turns tighten the spiral

params.name: Additional Degrees
params.does: extra twist in degrees on top of the whole rotations

params.name: ImageNode
params.does: internal image-node selector of the dialog (values not harvested)

pairs_with: Whirlpool (a smeared, fluid variant)
Ripple
a radial gradient overlay to focus the vortex centre

cards.non_destructive: yes from the Effects menu: CorelDRAW 2024 adds it to the object's effect stack; the scripted Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect path changes the bitmap itself

verified.note: The plate is twisted into one big clockwise spiral around the centre: the middle is wound into tight rings of dark, stripe and wall colours while the corners and the left swatches move least, like stirred paint.

cards.name: Tile
cards.summary: Repeats the whole image as a grid of smaller copies inside the original frame, like wallpaper; Horizontal and Vertical tiles set how many copies across and down. What Overlap and the unlabelled Square check box do to the grid was not established by the harvest.
use_for: wallpaper / contact-sheet style repeat of a photo or logo
pop-art grid poster from a single image
previewing how a texture repeats before making a pattern fill
avoid: many tiles shrink each copy until it is unreadable: keep to 2-6 per side for photos
a true seamless pattern fill: use a bitmap pattern fill, which repeats without resampling the image
the harvest's range binding for Vertical tiles points at MaxTilesPerRow (likely a UI-data quirk): stay within 1-100

params.name: Horizontal tiles
params.does: number of copies across

params.name: Vertical tiles
params.does: number of copies down

params.name: Overlap
params.does: percentage overlap of the tiles (exact behaviour not verified)

params.name: Square
params.does: unlabelled check box; presumably keeps the tiles square (not verified)

pairs_with: Offset (seam check for repeats)
a different colour adjustment per copy (PowerClip duplicates) for an Andy Warhol grid

cards.non_destructive: yes from the Effects menu: CorelDRAW 2024 adds it to the object's effect stack; the scripted Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect path changes the bitmap itself

verified.note: The whole plate is repeated as a 4 x 4 grid of smaller copies filling the original frame, like wallpaper or a contact sheet.

cards.name: Wet Paint
cards.summary: Makes the image look freshly painted and still wet, with colours running down in drips; Wetness picks which colours drip (positive values the lighter ones, negative the darker ones, per CorelDRAW help) and Percent sets the size of the drips.
use_for: horror / Halloween poster with dripping title art or photo
melting, running-paint look for street-art or grunge layouts
dripping product or ice-cream visual
avoid: small text drips into illegibility: apply to large display type or images only
a controlled single drip in a set place: draw it or use a drip brush, the effect drips everywhere the chosen tones are
on a pale, soft image light-colour drips are faint: try a negative Wetness to drip the dark areas

params.name: Wetness
params.does: which tones drip: positive values make lighter colours run, negative values darker ones; larger magnitude drips more

params.name: Percent
params.does: size / length of the drips

pairs_with: Wind (streaks in one direction)
a dark background so light drips stand out

cards.non_destructive: yes from the Effects menu: CorelDRAW 2024 adds it to the object's effect stack; the scripted Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect path changes the bitmap itself
